justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a mildly bearish to flat outlook across all three horizons, with the 1-day estimate at $205, drifting slightly lower to $204.50 at one week and $203 at one month. This gradual decline suggests I was anchoring to recent price momentum or a modest mean-reversion signal, likely reflecting some near-term overhead resistance or softening in whatever underlying asset this represents. The relatively tight clustering of estimates across horizons implies I saw no strong directional catalyst at the time of the forecast — the market appeared to be in a consolidation or modest drift-lower phase rather than trending sharply in either direction.

The confidence interval widths expand predictably as the time horizon lengthens, which is statistically appropriate. At one day, the 90% interval spans only $15 ($197.50 to $212.50), reflecting the relatively constrained intraday volatility typical of most liquid assets. By one week, that band widens to $33, and at one month it reaches $67 — roughly a 4x widening from daily to monthly. These widths were likely calibrated to historical realized volatility, where daily moves might average 1–2% and compound uncertainty over longer periods. Market microstructure noise, overnight gaps, and short-term sentiment shifts all contribute to the daily uncertainty, while macro data releases, earnings events, and broader risk appetite dominate at the weekly and monthly horizons.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the upside, a surprise positive catalyst — such as better-than-expected earnings, a favorable policy announcement, or a broader market rally — could drive the price well above $212.50 even within a single day. On the downside, a liquidity event, geopolitical shock, or sharp deterioration in macro conditions could easily breach the lower bound of $170 at the monthly horizon. Fat-tail risks are the primary concern here, as confidence intervals derived from normal or near-normal volatility assumptions tend to underweight the probability of sudden, large moves.

It is also worth noting that my one-month interval of $170 to $237 — while appearing wide in absolute terms — may still be too narrow if the asset in question is subject to binary events like regulatory decisions, clinical trial results, or major economic data surprises. Markets can gap significantly on such news, and historical volatility-based models systematically underestimate these jump risks. Any user of this forecast should treat the tails as softer boundaries than the 90% label implies, particularly at the monthly horizon.
